services.name: Whale Watching
services.desc: Every March and April, Ucluelet experiences the greatest whale migration on the planet. Up to 17,000 grey whales pass en route from their winter home on Mexico’s Baja Peninsula to the Arctic Ocean and Bering Sea - a journey of 22,530km/14,000mi. It’s the longest migration of any creature in the world. The greys can be 18m/66ft long, and are as buoyant as butterflies. Although March and April are the grey whale months in Ucluelet, whale-watching is available most of the year because of lingering pods of greys in Barkley Sound and through the Broken Group Islands, as well as growing numbers of humpback whales and resident killer or orca whales. services.name: Surf Lessons & Rentals
services.desc: Get your surf boards, wetsuits, and all the surfing gear you need to surf our famous West Coast beaches right on Long Beach! We’ll give you good advice on where to go and what the waves are doing. Book your surf lesson now and our surf instructors will have you surfing and smiling in no time! All our surf coaches are Native First Nation fully Certified Surf “Coaches” and local West Coast Instructors. We offer surf lessons and surf board and wetsuit rentals for all levels of experience. We can customize lessons for individual interest and we can also accommodate groups of up to 20

services.name: Fishing Charters
services.desc: The waters surrounding the Ucluth Peninsula offer some of the best salt water fishing in the Pacific Northwest and are rich in fishing history and culture. The ocean is full of nutrients which attract Chinook, Coho and Sockeye Salmon to the area. Halibut can be reeled in at some of the offshore banks and the shallow waters are excellent for fishing ling cod, red snapper and several species of rockfish. Crab traps can be dropped in the Ucluelet Harbour and shellfish can also be harvested nearby. services.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
services.desc: The Ucluelet Aquarium is truly a gem in this coastal community, giving visitors an up close and personal encounter with a diversity of local marine life. The touch tanks provide an interactive and fun, hands on, learning environment for children and adults. The displays are full of beautiful, interesting creatures and are always changing. Come and learn about the local marine ecosystems at the mini aquarium, and you’ll agree that there isn’t another aquarium like it! The aquarium is located in a brand new building and facility on the waterfront that opened in 2012. blurb: Experience the rugged, natural beauty of the west coast. Wya Point Resort rests on pristine, private beaches surrounded by 600 acres of old-growth forest on Ucluelet First Nation’s traditional territory, welcoming visitors with luxurious lodge accommodations, waterfront yurts and beachfront camping.
